Did the Multiplayer Online Battle Arena Kill Real-Time Strategy?
any article title that ends in a question is almost always answered with no

No, the repetitiveness of RTS games killed RTS. Just like the repetitiveness of FPS games is starting to kill them as well.

There's only so many ways you can re-skin resource management and battle strategy, just like there's only so many ways you can re-skin "shoot those guys!". People who like RTS will play already established titles that likely still have active communities and possibly even mods, and companies don't waste their time trying to crank out new games for a market that doesn't have much left in the well of inspiration.

I think the answer is actually partially yes.

RTS games except at the very highest level have never been about actual strategy but more about speed of execution. A genre of action games defined by an excessively obtuse interface, where most of what you'll be doing is fighting against that interface rather than against the enemy. MOBAs are in a way the quintessential RTS, finally dropping the strategic elements completely and expanding on the action. In that sense it is logical to see RTS games being replaced by MOBAs, as MOBAs largely do the same thing, just better.

Also yes, this analysis is not flattering, deal with it. Some people undoubtedly like RTS for the strategy even though I can't really fathom why they wouldn't play actual strategy games such as Civ, Paradox games, 4X stuff and so on.
If somebody could breed Total Annihilation with Alpha Centauri, they could have all money. I love the unit choices of TA and the strategy of AC.
The reason I can think of would be faster paced competition. A multiplayer game of Civ will take hours. A game of EU will take days.
Yes, it is clear that Starcraft is far more of a spectator's sport than Civ :D

Just want to point out, speed of execution is easily as important as planning when it comes to actual strategy. If you're up against a shit chess player, but they can make 2 moves to your one, you will probably get creamed even if you can see a dozen moves ahead.

"easily as important" is relative to the game. In games where it doesn't matter, it doesn't matter. Even in your own example you're not talking about speed of execution but about a turn time limit. That is fundamentally different as it doesn't have an impact on the mechanics. No chess game was ever lost because someone wasn't fast enough to pick up a piece and place it where they wanted, the sort of thing that happens frequently RTS.
Chess clocks and sudden death time limits
No. It's a subset of real-time strategy.

No, the real reason why real time strategy has been an ailing genre is because the games stopped being strategy games. Being able to shave seconds off your build order and micromanage units to get some ability into the exact right place at the exact right time is way more important than any actual strategy. Games only run for ten to twenty minutes, and base defenses aren't actually a deterrent to enemy forces so much as just something that buys you 10 seconds to get an army there when it's under attack.

Of course people who like those kinds of RTS games would much rather simply play a MOBA, which stresses all the same skills. People who actually want long drawn out matches that have multiple battles, strongholds that can withstand sieges, and win by attrition over who can consistently get the better kill ratios over the course of a two hour game on the other hand don't really have any games to call their own anymore.

**Daily Devotional**

**April 27**

*11 Wherefore also we pray always for you, that our God would count you worthy of this calling, and fulfil all the good pleasure of his goodness, and the work of faith with power: 12 That the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and ye in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ. (2 Thessalonians 1:11-12 KJV)*

Paul is praying that the Thessalonians would be worthy of God’s calling to be His children. We should all try our best to be worthy of God’s calling on our lives, as He gave His only Son to save us, and the least we can do is try to be worthy of His love for us (Romans 12:1). Our religious teaching does not even tell us of our having faith with power. We are taught that we are just saved from hell, and nothing about the power of God that is put inside us, the same power that raised Christ from the dead (Ephesians 1:19-20). We need to learn of this power we have, and use it. How can Jesus be glorified in us, and us in Him, if we don’t even know what He has given us in our born again spirits?

All Christians need to renew their minds with the Word of God (Romans 12:2), and learn just what we have in our new spirits. We not only have power over the devil (James 4:7), but over sickness (1 Peter 2:24), diseases (Psalms 103:3), poverty (3 John 1:2), depression (Isaiah 26:3), etc. If Christians would just learn how to use what we have, we would live the victorious life that Jesus purchased for us, now in this world, and do the things He told us to do (John 14:12). Praise God for giving us such power.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
